summary.headline: Infusion Pump Procurement: Scoring Timeline and Payment Records Review
summary.overview: This brief summarizes documented records concerning the infusion pump replacement procurement, including bid closure, scoring instructions and final award, alongside reporter allegations regarding the scoring process and related payments.
key_points: Bids for the infusion pump replacement closed on 17 Feb 2026, with the scoring committee scheduled to meet on 3 March to finalise weights and scores [C001, C002].
PERSON_1 instructed PERSON_5 to update the technical score for ORG_2 from 61 to 78 before the sheet went to PERSON_4, which PERSON_5 communicated to others as PERSON_1 wanting 61 -> 78 [C003, C005].
PERSON_1 stated the committee had already agreed verbally so there was no need to recirculate the score sheet [C004].

At the time of the request to raise ORG_2's score, the scoring committee had not yet met, with PERSON_1 also reported as saying if the score was not bumped the pumps would slip another quarter [C007, C006].

A meeting was held on 10 March 2026 attended by PERSON_1 as chair, PERSON_5 and PERSON_6, which recorded final technical scores as ORG_2 78 and ORG_4 74 and recommended award of the infusion pump contract (est. value $1.2M) to ORG_2 [C008, C009, C010].
The meeting record notes no conflicts of interest were declared, and PERSON_4 as Chief Financial Officer approved the award on 14 March 2026 [C011, C012].
Two payments of $18,500 to ORG_3 for consulting retainer - procurement advisory on 2026-03-20 and 2026-04-20 were approved by PERSON_1 [C013, C017].
Reporter alleges being told in early March by a colleague that PERSON_1 had asked for ORG_2's technical score to be raised before the committee met [C014].

Reporter alleges observing two $18,500 payments to ORG_3 for consulting after the contract was signed and finding no consulting agreement, and states a belief that ORG_3 is connected to PERSON_1's husband PERSON_3 but acknowledges having no documents to show this [C015, C016].
risk_notes: Timing gap between documented instruction to raise score and committee meeting raises process documentation questions.
Recorded statement of verbal agreement without recirculation contrasts with record that committee had not yet met at time of instruction.
Payments to ORG_3 approved by same individual involved in scoring instruction, with reporter allegation of missing consulting agreement and unverified connection claim.
limitations: No independent documentary evidence was provided to verify the alleged verbal agreement or the reason for the score change beyond the quoted statements.
No documents were provided to establish a connection between ORG_3 and PERSON_3; the reporter explicitly states no documents show this.
No consulting agreement was located in the supplied evidence, but absence of evidence is not evidence of absence and no independent proof of payment purpose was provided.
Evidence does not show intent, authorization basis for payments, or whether procurement policies were violated; no legal conclusions can be drawn from the records alone.

To: EMAIL_2
Date: 18 Feb 2026
Subject: Infusion pump RFP — evaluation timeline Team — bids for the infusion pump replacement closed yesterday. The scoring committee will meet on March 3 to finalise weights and scores. Please do not share technical scores with vendors before then. — PERSON_1, Director of Procurement
PERSON_5 — please update the technical score for ORG_2 from 61 to 78 before the sheet goes to PERSON_4 on Friday. The committee already agreed verbally, so no need to recirculate. Thanks, PERSON_1

[09:12] PERSON_5: did you see the email from PERSON_1 yesterday
[09:13] [REDACTED]: the one about medaxis?
[09:13] PERSON_5: yeah she wants 61 -> 78 [09:15] PERSON_5: she said if we dont bump it the pumps will slip another quarter
[09:16] [REDACTED]: the committee hasnt even met yet
[09:16] PERSON_5: i know.

Meeting held 10 March 2026. Present: PERSON_1 (chair), PERSON_5, PERSON_6. Final technical scores: ORG_2 78, ORG_4 74. Price scores were taken from the bid summary without change. Recommendation: award the infusion pump contract (est. value $1.2M) to ORG_2. The committee notes no conflicts of interest were declared.
Approved for award: PERSON_4, Chief Financial Officer, 14 March 2026.

follow_up_questions.question: What is the exact date and time of the instruction to update the technical score for ORG_2 from 61 to 78, and what transmission records (e.g., email headers, system logs) could confirm when it was sent relative to the committee meeting on 10 March 2026?
follow_up_questions.rationale: Claims C003, C005, C007 and C008 have unresolved or imprecise dates; establishing the precise timing is needed to determine whether the instruction occurred before the committee met and before the scheduled 3 March meeting.

follow_up_questions.question: What contemporaneous records, if any, exist to document the stated verbal agreement of the committee that no recirculation was needed, such as meeting notes, emails, or attestations from committee members?
follow_up_questions.rationale: C004 relies on a single statement that the committee already agreed verbally; no corroborating record is cited, and C007 indicates the committee had not yet met at the time of the request, creating uncertainty about what agreement occurred and when.

follow_up_questions.question: How were the final technical scores of 78 for ORG_2 and 74 for ORG_4 determined and documented, and what scoring sheets, evaluation criteria, or individual evaluator records support the change from 61 to 78?
follow_up_questions.rationale: C003 and C009 show a score increase from 61 to 78 without documented methodology; understanding the scoring process and supporting worksheets would help distinguish between a documented re-evaluation and an unsupported adjustment.

follow_up_questions.question: What contractual or deliverable records exist for the two $18,500 payments to ORG_3 on 2026-03-20 and 2026-04-20, such as a consulting agreement, scope of work, invoices, or approval justifications?
follow_up_questions.rationale: C013 and C017 document payments approved by PERSON_1, while C015 alleges no consulting agreement could be found; identifying whether such records exist would address the missing-records gap.

follow_up_questions.question: What verifiable records, if any, could confirm or refute a connection between ORG_3 and PERSON_3, such as corporate registration, ownership, or disclosure filings, without relying on belief alone?
follow_up_questions.rationale: C016 is an unverifiable allegation with no documents, and C011 notes no conflicts were declared; objective records are needed to assess the alleged relationship while preserving uncertainty.

follow_up_questions.question: What additional records could corroborate the early March communication in which a colleague reportedly relayed that a score increase had been requested before the committee met?
follow_up_questions.rationale: C014 is a hearsay allegation with moderate confidence and no independent document support; identifying any contemporaneous messages, logs, or witness accounts could help assess its reliability without assuming misconduct.
